items.followUp: Explain five careers that use knowledge of biology.

rubric.why: Explains how biological knowledge is used in medicine.
rubric.description: Links medicine with understanding the body, diagnosing disease, or treating patients.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant explanation of medicine as a profession.

rubric.why: Explains a biological application in crop production.
rubric.description: Links agriculture with growing or improving crops, or controlling pests or plant diseases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant explanation of agriculture.

rubric.why: Explains the use of biology in animal care and production.
rubric.description: Links animal husbandry with breeding, rearing, or caring for animals or livestock.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant explanation of animal husbandry.

rubric.why: Explains a biological career involving fish or aquatic resources.
rubric.description: Links fisheries with breeding or rearing fish, or managing fish resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant explanation of fisheries.

rubric.why: Explains a biological career involving forests.
rubric.description: Links forestry with management, conservation, or study of forests.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant explanation of forestry.

modelAnswer: Medicine: Biology helps doctors understand the human body, diagnose diseases, and treat patients.
Agriculture: Biological knowledge is used to grow crops, improve varieties, and control pests and plant diseases.
Animal husbandry: Biology is used to breed, rear, and care for useful animals and livestock.
Fisheries: Knowledge of aquatic organisms is used to breed and rear fish and manage fish resources.
Forestry: Biology helps in the management, conservation, and study of forests and their organisms.

items.followUp: State the aims of biological classification and name characteristics used as its basis.

rubric.why: Gives an aim of classification: identification or making the study of organisms easier and systematic.
rubric.description: States that classification helps identify organisms or makes their study easier and more systematic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either valid aim.

rubric.why: Explains how classification helps avoid confusion in naming and identification.
rubric.description: States that classification helps avoid confusion caused by different common names or aids identification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this additional aim.

rubric.why: Identifies showing relationships as an aim of classification.
rubric.description: States that classification helps show relationships among organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct relationship-based aim.

rubric.why: States the general basis for grouping organisms.
rubric.description: States that organisms are grouped by comparing similarities and differences in their characteristics.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this general basis.

rubric.why: Names suitable characteristics used to compare and classify organisms.
rubric.description: Gives at least one valid characteristic used as a basis for classification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any suitable example.

modelAnswer: Classification is the arrangement of organisms into groups according to their similarities and differences.
Its aims include making the study of the great variety of organisms easier and more systematic.
It helps in identifying organisms and avoiding confusion caused by different common names.
It helps show relationships among organisms, including their evolutionary relationships.
Organisms are classified by comparing characteristics such as morphology, anatomy, cell structure, and other biological features.

items.followUp: Explain how light intensity, humidity, and wind affect the rate of transpiration.

rubric.why: Explains the effect of temperature on water loss from leaves.
rubric.description: States that higher temperature generally increases transpiration by increasing evaporation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct effect and direction.

rubric.why: Explains how atmospheric moisture affects the water-vapour gradient.
rubric.description: States that high humidity reduces transpiration or dry air increases it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct effect of humidity.

rubric.why: Explains the effect of moving air around the leaf.
rubric.description: States that wind removes moist air near the leaf and generally increases transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct effect or explanation.

rubric.why: Explains how light affects stomatal opening and water loss.
rubric.description: States that light usually opens stomata and increases transpiration, or that darkness tends to close stomata.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct light-related effect.

rubric.why: Includes an additional factor and its effect on transpiration.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of water availability or leaf area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct additional factor and effect.

modelAnswer: Temperature: A rise in temperature increases evaporation from leaf surfaces and generally increases transpiration.
Humidity: High humidity reduces transpiration because the difference in water-vapour concentration between the leaf and air is smaller; dry air increases it.
Wind: Wind removes moist air around the leaf, maintaining a steep diffusion gradient and generally increasing transpiration.
Light: Light usually causes stomata to open, increasing water loss; in darkness stomata tend to close and transpiration falls.
Water supply and leaf features also affect the rate: water shortage may cause stomata to close, while a larger leaf area generally allows more transpiration.
